title: Great Source of Life and Light
description: Great Source of Life and Light in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 1001 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For a Holy Heart”, where the book credits them to a Wesleyan source.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great Source of life and light, Thy heav-enly grace im-part, And by thy ho-ly spir-it_ write Thy law up-on my heart. My soul would cleave to thee; Let nought my pur-pose move; O, let my faith more stead-fast be, And more in-tense my love!

lines: Great Source of life and light,
And by thy holy spirit write
My soul would cleave to thee;
O, let my faith more steadfast be,
Long as the cross I bear,
O, let my soul on thee be cast
Where storm and tempest rise no more,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
